angle: WR/TE route-cut mechanics from Combine route drills (Break G), graded by the same code on NFL route families and tested against full-season separation over expected (SOE) on held-out draft classes, with straight-line speed as the benchmark that does carry; last season's SOE as a day-3 lean (not a proven rule); 2026 GO/HOLD film-priority flags.
metric_name: Break G: how hard a receiver brakes into and drives out of his sharpest cut, as a share of body weight, measured at 10 Hz (z within drill and Combine year, reliability-shrunk; 1 sd = 0.021 g).
headline_number: -1.2 in of season SOE per sd of Break G [90%: -3.6, +1.0], n=116 receivers in unseen classes; one hierarchical model (receiver and class random effects, 167 player-seasons) gives -0.5 [-2.8, +1.8]. Speed benchmark on the same 90 receivers: official 40 vs NFL top speed rho 0.46 [0.32, 0.58] vs Break G -0.02 [-0.20, 0.16]. Day 3 is a lean: pre-registered gain 0.31 [-0.08, 0.63], p 0.12; pre-set gap-32 override +5.9 in [-6.1, +20.0], p 0.22.
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_19/cand_2 applying the round-19 judges. Lede is the Break G null alone, in plain words; the +7.4 in any-gap override moved out of the lede and labelled 'chosen after seeing data'; the pre-set gap-32 rule is the primary row; title and rule 3 softened ('lean, then check film'; no 'whatever the pick gap'). New analyses: (1) speed benchmark on the same n as the Break G scatter and a reconciliation of pooled raw WR+TE 0.73 vs 0.46 within position and year (TE 0.23 s slower in the 40, 1.1 yd/s slower in games); (2) one mixed model for the Break G slope with receiver and class random effects (-0.5 [-2.8, +1.8], class variance 0, TOST p 0.04, appendix); (3) nested override test that re-chooses the pick-gap threshold on contrasts sharing neither receiver (+9.1 [-2.5, +18.2], p 0.11) -- grafted from the runner-up DL candidate's nested back-test idea; (4) informative back-test on every day-3 pair (top half by SOE vs pick-only: 5/10 vs 5/10, difference 0 [-33, +21], MDE 42 pts) plus the MDE of the rank gain (0.55); (5) one pooled coverage- and alignment-adjusted film SOE per 2026 name (39-40 snaps each) replacing 24 split cells; (6) simulated game-speed rerun (drill reps re-priced at NFL entry speed): rank corr 0.91 with the current score, still no transfer (-0.05), re-grades none of the six 2026 names, so the drill recommendation is 'add reps before speed' (reliability 0.53 -> 0.62). Writeup: ~1,756 words (was 1,977); Table 1 cut to 4 rows; Table 2 is 3 plain rows with one-sided p; 'What flips each name' paragraph and split columns removed; sensitivity grid and TOST moved to the appendix; 'Bottom line' after the results. Viz: Fig 1 = side-by-side speed and Break G scatters on identical axes (same 90 receivers) + enlarged trace panel with gaps in titles, 'How to read' text removed; Fig 2 retitled and gains a mixed-model row; Fig 3 shared yard scale, pink drill path (distinct from amber HOLD), entry-speed bars, rerun shift per name; Fig 4 = dumbbell + one decision panel in inches with a catches axis and break-even line (gain forest dropped); Fig 5 drop-off marker labelled in words, decision date printed, marker size = sampled snaps with size key.
open_risks: The day-3 evidence is a lean only: every override interval crosses zero (pre-set p 0.22) and the back-test is underpowered (MDE 42 pts); judges may see the 2026 list as resting on little.
The hierarchical model is in-sample, unweighted and restricted to 50+ route seasons; its TOST p 0.04 should not be read as held-out equivalence (held-out TOST p 0.10).
The game-speed rerun is simulated from a within-drill linear slope of Break G on entry speed; no drill was run at game speed.
Film SOE and Fig 3 rest on sampled NFL plays (up to 40 per player, half top-EPA); Troy Franklin is GO by rule although his pooled film SOE is -17 in [-34, 0].
9 figures and tables in total is at the limit.
